cards.title: Sparse Sampling Data Handling and Bias Conditions
cards.claim: For sparse destructive sampling, Phoenix calculates PK parameters from a mean concentration curve derived from unique time points. The Phoenix sparse estimator generates unbiased estimates for batch designs only if equal sample sizes are present per time point; unequal n introduces bias in this specific implementation. Standard errors for AUC (SE_AUClast/SE_AUCall) are computed using linear trapezoidal rules and account for correlations from repeated sampling, but are not output if log trapezoidal rules are specified.
conditions: Data structure must support grouping by unique time points (nominal time recommended).
AUC calculation must use linear trapezoidal rules for SE_AUC computation to be valid.
Equal sample sizes per time point are required for unbiased parameter estimates in batch designs.
required_inputs: Individual subject data with time and concentration.
Subject IDs to calculate correlations for repeated sampling.
Explicit selection of linear trapezoidal rule for AUC calculation.
limitations: Nominal time grouping is a software recommendation for sparse analysis, not a universal substitution rule for actual times.
SE_AUC calculations depend on AUC being a linear combination of mean concentrations; invalid for log-trapezoidal methods.
Missing data in the dataset prevents unbiased estimates in sparse routines.
cards.downstream_use: Use mean-curve parameters for group-level PK characterization. Verify design balance (equal n) before interpreting sparse PK estimates. Do not use log-trapezoidal AUC if SE_AUC is required.
cards.retrieval_keywords: NCA endpoints with unreliable terminal slope and sparse destructive sampling

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
